gen-gf-baloo-thambi-2-fs-paquito: Expressive and a bit goofy-deep in the lowercase, Baloo Thambi 2 takes the heading spot with distinct gaps in its c, e and s. Paquito follows as a confident serif whose small letters sit close to the capitals, built for brief, easy reading.
gen-gf-balsamiq-sans-gf-epunda-slab: Epunda Slab reads dignified and a touch old-fashioned, its rounded lowercase standing tall with a visibly gaping c. Balsamiq Sans above it keeps one steady line weight with no pinched curves, so the heading feels loose against that text serif.
gen-gf-balsamiq-sans-gf-fauna-one: Lines bent like rope or tubing, with no pinched curves, make Balsamiq Sans instantly recognizable. It is loud and expressive up top, while Fauna One, a literary serif with a tall middle band and short ascenders, stays quiet underneath.
gen-gf-balsamiq-sans-gf-glegoo: Balsamiq Sans bends its strokes like a bent steel rod, bold and expressive without a single pinched curve. Shrink it, though, and that chunky character thins out, while Glegoo, a classic serif with big counters and open mouths, holds up at larger sizes too.
gen-gf-balsamiq-sans-gf-hanuman: A laser-cut sheet look, one cutting width throughout, gives Balsamiq Sans its bold, expressive face. Hanuman steps in below as a traditional serif with a high-waisted lowercase and wide-set terminals on the s, refined where the heading is blunt.
gen-gf-balsamiq-sans-gf-kadwa: Round, tubular and bold, with bowls that never swell or taper. Kadwa follows as a classic serif with open-ended curves and a larger-than-usual x-height, and that mix of rounded heading and editorial text is the pair's real draw.
gen-gf-balsamiq-sans-gf-noticia-text: Noticia Text reads literary and dignified, with big entrances into its curves. Over a long page it would feel full and steady, a serif with tall lowercase bodies under Balsamiq Sans, whose heavy lines carry no thin hairline at all.
gen-gf-balsamiq-sans-gf-piazzolla: Piazzolla is refined and authoritative, its lowercase nearly matching the capitals. Balsamiq Sans is the one for bold, expressive headings with no pinched curves, while that classic serif does its best work as a tall, open e-shaped body.
gen-gf-balsamiq-sans-gf-pridi: Refined and classic, Pridi gives its small letters a proud, almost capital-sized stance with generous space between curve ends and the stem. Against bold, bendy Balsamiq Sans, the serif's height is the pair's strongest quality.
gen-gf-balsamiq-sans-gf-scope-one: No thin strokes ever vanish in Balsamiq Sans, which stays bold and expressive. Scope One brings the opposite: a classic serif with a big x-height and stubby ascenders, and its counters spilling into the space around them is what makes this pair stand out.
